craft_notes: Sthāyin: śānta-vīra of non-difference; vyabhicāri peace at pair undivided. Sanskrit-first: abhinna (UNPARTED — kept ‘never part’); abheda (NO-SPLIT — kept; two negations, kept two); tattvatas (IN-TRUTH — kept, twice-grounded). Rows: 9 (never-part + no-split — doubled non-difference), 1 (‘no split’ closes — abheda last, twice-said), 3 (bondage/release × nature/Lord interlock: 1-with-3, 2-with-4). Close: ‘there is no split’. Rupture: semicolon (pair-unity turns to Lord-unity). Rejected: ‘are one’ — killed: two negations kept two; ‘in God’ — killed: Lord kept (house diction); ‘essentially’ for ‘in truth’ — killed: tattvatas kept. Read aloud: BOND-age AND re-LEASE, BOTH from the LORD's-own-NA-ture, NEV-er PART … IN-truth, IN the LORD, there IS no SPLIT.

lines: Bondage and release, both from the Lord's own nature, never part;
in truth, in the Lord, there is no split.
l4.sanskrit_cite: etau bandhavimokṣau ca parameśasvarūpataḥ | na bhidyete na bhedo hi tattvataḥ parameśvare

reads_against.argmap: Do bondage and release differ? → Double non-difference: of the pair, and in the Lord, in truth.
c1_essence: Bondage-release undivided in nature and Lord, in truth.
